title: VRAM budget math: weights, activations, caches

questions.q: You double the image's side. What happens to ComfyUI's working memory estimate?
options: Nothing, it depends on the file
questions.why: The estimate is proportional to latent height times width, and both doubled.

questions.q: You double the batch. What happens to the weights on the card?
questions.why: One copy of the model serves the batch. Working memory doubles, weights do not.

questions.q: Why is a model's file size not enough to tell you it fits?
options: Working memory, reserved memory and a 10% margin come on top
The file is compressed about tenfold
Files on disk use different units from VRAM
questions.answer: Working memory, reserved memory and a 10% margin come on top
questions.why: load_models_gpu asks for model size × 1.1 + extra_mem.

questions.q: SDXL and SD3 at 1024 px have the same latent side, 128. Why does SD3's estimate come out twice as large?
options: Its latent has 16 channels, and channels count
questions.why: Channels are not in this formula. The factor differs per family.

questions.q: Where does a finished latent wait for the next node, by default?
options: On the card, next to the weights
On disk in the temp folder
questions.why: intermediate_device returns the CPU unless --gpu-only is set.

questions.q: How much should you trust memory_required as a peak?
options: It is an estimate, and its source says it needs tweaking
It is measured live from the card
It is always an exact upper limit
questions.answer: It is an estimate, and its source says it needs tweaking
questions.why: The comment in model_base.py says so, and this lesson did not compare it with a measured peak.
